issues.description: Return type of Stock.take(String) is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML specifies Stock.take(String): int, the solution implementation defines take(String) returning int (using -1 as failure), but the template repository's Stock.take currently returns boolean. This mismatch can confuse students about which return value to check (boolean vs. int sentinel) and may block following the reference solution or UML instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Stock.take(String) method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the template implementation to return int (using -1 to indicate missing/insufficient ingredient) to match the UML and the solution, and document the expected sentinel behavior. Alternatively, if a boolean design is intended, update the UML and solution to use boolean and adjust code examples accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement UML specifies Stock.take(String): int (returns an int), but the template implementation declares public boolean take(String) (returns boolean). The solution implements take as returning int. This mismatch in the return type for the same conceptual operation (taking an ingredient from stock) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the exercise and UML expect an int-returning method, but the starter code exposes a boolean, forcing them to resolve a type mismatch before implementing SealSaloon logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem UML and the solution by changing the template method signature to 'public int take(String ingredient)' and updating its implementation to return -1 when the ingredient does not exist or quantity is insufficient, otherwise return the remaining quantity. This keeps the method name and semantics consistent across the problem, template, and solution.
